card.title: Ask Around the Missing Detail
card.instruction: Find one hidden fact by asking about everything surrounding it and never naming it directly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Was that extra dinner plate for someone who eats meat?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why don't you ask who came over?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I am only checking what leftovers we still have.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They ate the last of your mushroom pie.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And the filling? Did that get eaten too, or are there mushrooms hidden under the napkin?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 dietary question circles identity; A3 claims leftover inventory; A5 probes selective eating after B2 names the hidden visitor question.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 who challenge prompts A3 cover; B4 mushroom pie prompts A5 whether filling was avoided.

relationship.evidence: B2 recognizes the real inquiry and B4 supplies an ordinary food detail.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 mushroom content to seek a more discriminating clue about the guest.

specificity.evidence: A1 extra plate and B2 visitor make the hidden fact legible while A asks only surrounding food questions.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 mushrooms under a napkin makes covert fact-finding specific rather than decorative riddling.
